$about: Machine-side knob for the performance gate. The real floor for each
scenario lives in tests/scenarios/<name>.json under expects.
min_ticks_per_second, so a scenario can never drift away from the
performance contract it was written to hold.
floor_multiplier scales every floor at once — set it below 1.0 on a slow
CI box rather than weakening the scenarios themselves.
overrides pins one scenario to an absolute floor, before the multiplier.
$measured_baseline: IT IS LEFT AT 1.0 DELIBERATELY, AND THE GATE IS RED BECAUSE OF IT. Read
this before anyone reaches for the knob.
The perf stage is red on this Linux container for both scenarios. It is
NOT a regression from the seven-builder wave. A/B, measured by the
integrator alone on a quiet box (0 other Godot processes, verified before
and after every reading), three readings each:
scenario      pre-wave afb031b     post-wave (this tree)    floor
The floors were met when they were set — the record says stress_1000 went
36 -> 122..144 ticks/s and the floor was raised 35 -> 100 on the strength
of it. This box does 75 before a single line of the wave landed. So the
gap between 75 and 100 is the machine, and the ~3% between 76 and 74 is
the wave. Both numbers are in the same column and only one of them is a
regression anybody can fix by writing code.
Lowering floor_multiplier here would turn the stage green in one line and
would also hide the next real regression, because a 25% cushion is wider
than most regressions worth catching. The honest options are to run the
gate on the machine the floors describe, or to re-derive the floors on the
machine that will run it, with the readings above as the starting point.
That is a decision about what this build promises, so it is Maximilian's
and not the integrator's.
Measured 2026-08-15, Godot 4.7.1, 4 cores, llvmpipe. Headless: these are
simulation throughput numbers and no renderer is involved.
